draft.title: Text structure follows purpose
card: Writers build a text to suit its purpose. The purpose is why the text exists, such as to judge, to persuade or to inform. The order of the parts helps the text do its job.
a review first says what the text is about. It then gives a judgement, with details from the text to back it up.
a persuasive text first states a position. It then gives reasons to support it and ends by summing up the position.
A reader who knows the usual order can find the parts quickly and can see how the writer is trying to reach them.
draft.remember: Writers order the parts of a text so that it can do its job.

a.q: Why does a persuasive text usually give its reasons after stating the position?
opts: The reasons then support a position the reader already knows
The reasons are the summing up that ends the text
The reasons tell the reader what the text is about
The reasons let the writer avoid stating a position
a.why: A persuasive text states its position first, so the reasons that follow have something to support. The reasons are not the summing up, because the text ends by sums up the position, not by adding new reasons.
a.clue: Think about what the reasons are meant to support.

b.q: Jai writes a review of a film. Which order of parts best suits a review?
opts: What the film is about, then a judgement backed by details
A judgement first, then a plan to persuade the reader to act
Reasons to see the film, then a position, then a summing up
A summing up first, then what the film is about
b.why: A review first tells readers what the text is about, then gives a judgement backed by details from the text. The reasons-then-position order is wrong because a position comes first in a persuasive text, and a summing up comes at the end.
b.clue: A reader needs to know what is being judged before the judgement.

a.best: The reasons then support a position the reader already knows

b.best: What the film is about, then a judgement backed by details

problems.detail: The clue ('Think about what the reasons are meant to support') repeats the word 'support', which appears only in the right option. A student could match the word without knowing the idea.
The right option is clearly the longest, and it is the only one with an extra qualifying detail ('the reader already knows'), so it stands out from the other options.
The why has a grammar error: 'the text ends by sums up the position' should be 'the text ends by summing up the position'.
